titleEn: El Niño is threatening California’s fragile coast again – the 1982-83 El Niño opened eyes to the serious erosion risks
titleZh: 厄尔尼诺再度威胁加州海岸：1982—1983 年的侵蚀教训
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: California’s coastal bluffs and beaches look rugged, but they can be surprisingly fragile in the face of a powerful El Niño.
paragraphs.zh: 加州的海岸悬崖和海滩看起来崎岖不平，但在强大的厄尔尼诺现象面前，它们可能会令人惊讶地脆弱。

paragraphs.en: The state saw that in 1982-83, when storms amid one of the most destructive El Niño winters in California history battered the coastline with powerful waves and torrential rain, leaving hundreds of millions of dollars in damage in its wake. The storms coincided with elevated sea levels, high astronomical tides and very large waves delivered by repeated storms.
paragraphs.zh: 1982年至1983年，加利福尼亚州经历了加州历史上最具破坏性的厄尔尼诺冬季之一，风暴伴随着强大的海浪和暴雨袭击了海岸线，造成数亿美元的损失。风暴发生时，海平面上升，天文潮汐高涨，反复出现的风暴带来了巨大的海浪。

paragraphs.en: Extreme waves that winter destroyed one-third of the Santa Monica Pier and tore off large sections of the Huntington Beach Pier and the Paradise Cove Pier, while also damaging the Seal Beach, San Clemente and Malibu piers. Numerous seawalls, decks and stairways were torn apart, and 33 oceanfront homes were destroyed.
paragraphs.zh: 那年冬天的极端海浪摧毁了圣莫尼卡码头的三分之一，摧毁了亨廷顿海滩码头和天堂湾码头的大部分，同时也破坏了海豹滩、圣克莱门特和马里布码头。许多海堤、甲板和楼梯被撕裂，33座海滨房屋被摧毁。

paragraphs.en: Massive waves also stripped millions of cubic yards of sand from Southern California beaches, and sections of the Pacific Coast Highway suffered severe flooding, mudslides and washouts.
paragraphs.zh: 巨浪还从南加州海滩上剥离了数百万立方码的沙子，太平洋海岸公路的部分路段遭受了严重的洪水，泥石流和冲刷。

paragraphs.en: Along the central coast, waves and high-tide flooding eroded bluffs. In Pacifica, just outside San Francisco, the edge of a sandy cliff lost over 65 feet as it failed, collapsing onto the beach and forcing the relocation of a two-story building and removal of an entire row of mobile homes. This area of high but weak bluffs continued to erode over the subsequent decades, forcing the demolition of bluff-top homes and apartments.
paragraphs.zh: 沿着中部海岸，海浪和涨潮的洪水侵蚀了悬崖。在旧金山弗朗西斯科外的帕西菲卡，一座桑迪悬崖的边缘坍塌了65英尺（约合10米），坍塌在海滩上，迫使一栋两层楼的建筑搬迁，一整排移动的房屋也被拆除。在随后的几十年里，这片高耸但脆弱的悬崖继续受到侵蚀，迫使他们拆除悬崖顶的房屋和公寓。

paragraphs.en: The El Niño now building in 2026-27 is forecast to be even stronger, and coastal homes are already seeing damage. I have studied coastal geology and oceanography in California for nearly six decades. With the conditions expected this year, coastal flooding, coastal erosion and landslides are likely, and more dramatic cliff collapses wouldn’t be a surprise, though every El Niño is different.
paragraphs.zh: 据预测，2026- 2027年正在形成的厄尔尼诺现象会更加强烈，沿海地区的房屋已经受到了破坏。我在加州研究海岸地质和海洋学已经将近60年了。根据今年的预期情况，海岸洪水、海岸侵蚀和山体滑坡都有可能发生，更严重的悬崖崩塌也不足为奇，尽管每次厄尔尼诺现象都不一样。

paragraphs.en: What is El Niño and why is it so destructive?
paragraphs.zh: 什么是厄尔尼诺现象，为什么它如此具有破坏性？

paragraphs.en: El Niño is one end of a climate pattern that swings from warm to cold every few years and can change weather patterns around the world. Normally dry areas can experience flooding rains, and wet areas can suffer droughts. The U.S. Pacific Coast in particular can take a beating from powerful atmospheric river storms with heavy downpours.
paragraphs.zh: 厄尔尼诺现象是气候模式的一端，每隔几年就会从温暖到寒冷，并且可以改变世界各地的天气模式。通常干旱地区会经历洪水，潮湿地区会遭受干旱。美国太平洋海岸特别容易受到强大的大气河流风暴的打击，带来倾盆大雨。

paragraphs.en: El Niños begin with a shift in wind patterns, which normally push warm waters from east to west along the equator. For reasons still not fully understood, the trade winds die and the warm pool of water in the western Pacific begins to flow back toward the coast of South America.
paragraphs.zh: 厄尔尼诺现象开始于风向的转变，通常会将温暖的沃茨沿着赤道从东向西推。由于尚不完全清楚的原因，信风消失，西太平洋的暖水池开始向南美洲海岸回流。

paragraphs.en: Part of this warm mass moves north toward the coast of California as a pulse or bulge, known as a Kelvin wave, and it begins to have far-ranging impacts.
paragraphs.zh: 这一温暖的物质的一部分向北移动到加州海岸作为脉冲或隆起，被称为开尔文波，它开始产生深远的影响。

paragraphs.en: Seawater expands as it warms, which raises sea level along the Pacific Coast for weeks during these periodic events. While all El Niños are not created equal, during the very large 1982-83 event, sea levels were elevated above predicted high tides by about a foot in San Diego to nearly 2 feet in San Francisco.
paragraphs.zh: 海水在变暖时膨胀，在这些周期性事件中，这会使太平洋沿岸的海平面沿着上升数周。虽然所有的厄尔尼诺现象都不是一样的，但在1982-83年的特大事件中，海平面在圣地亚哥比预测的高潮高出约1英尺，在旧金山弗朗西斯科高出近2英尺。

paragraphs.en: These higher sea levels can reach higher elevations and last longer.
paragraphs.zh: 这些更高的海平面可以到达更高的海拔，持续更长的时间。

paragraphs.en: The elevated sea levels also allow storm waves to break closer to the shoreline, eroding beaches and bluffs, leading to damage and destruction of both private oceanfront development and public infrastructure, including streets and highways, bridges and piers, and parks and recreational facilities.
paragraphs.zh: 海平面上升还使风暴波浪更接近海岸线，侵蚀海滩和悬崖，导致私人海滨开发和公共基础设施，包括街道和高速公路，桥梁和码头以及公园和娱乐设施遭到破坏和破坏。

paragraphs.en: Why California is vulnerable
paragraphs.zh: 为什么加州是脆弱的

paragraphs.en: Much of California’s coastal and shoreline development took place from the late 1940s to the late 1970s when the state’s population exploded.
paragraphs.zh: 加州的大部分沿海和海岸线开发都发生在20世纪40年代末到70年代末，当时该州人口激增。

paragraphs.en: Homes were built on beaches, bluffs and dunes during a period when the coastal storm climate was generally mild and there were no real concerns with coastal hazards and future sea-level rise.
paragraphs.zh: 房屋建在海滩、悬崖和沙丘上，当时沿海风暴气候一般比较温和，对沿海灾害和未来海平面上升没有真实的担忧。

paragraphs.en: This changed quickly in 1978 when the first strong El Niño in recent memory arrived, raising alarm about the hazards ocean development was exposed to.
paragraphs.zh: 这种情况在1978年迅速改变，当时出现了最近记忆中第一次强烈的厄尔尼诺现象，引起了人们对海洋开发所面临的危险的警觉。

paragraphs.en: The extreme 1982-83 El Niño that followed a few years later caused about US$328 million (in 2025 dollars) in damage to oceanfront property, $87 million in losses to recreational facilities such as piers, parking lots and access stairs, and $66 million in damage to large engineering structures such as breakwaters and jetties designed to protect harbors from storm waves.
paragraphs.zh: 1982年至1983年的极端厄尔尼诺现象在几年后造成了约3.28亿美元（2025年美元）的海滨财产损失，8700万美元的码头，停车场和楼梯等娱乐设施损失，以及6600万美元的大型工程结构损失，如防波堤和码头，旨在保护港口免受风暴波的影响。

paragraphs.en: At least in the short term, the 1982-83 El Niño winter changed popular perceptions of the stability or security of oceanfront homes and other shoreline development. Building restrictions were tightened, insurance rates rose, and many requests for new seawall permits were submitted.
paragraphs.zh: 至少在短期内，1982年至1983年的厄尔尼诺冬季改变了人们对海滨住宅和其他海岸开发的稳定性或安全性的看法，建筑限制收紧，保险费率上升，许多人提出了新海堤许可证的申请。

paragraphs.en: But then it was back to business as usual, as new arrivals to the coast outbid each other for the same oceanfront homes damaged a few years before.
paragraphs.zh: 但后来又恢复了正常，因为新来的人竞相竞购几年前受损的海滨住宅。

paragraphs.en: Increased coastal armoring, such as seawalls and rock revetments, helped limit erosion during other very large El Niños that followed, in 1997-98 and 2015-16, along with lucky timing that large waves arrived at low points in the monthly tidal cycle, leading to significantly less property damage than in 1982-83.
paragraphs.zh: 海堤和岩石护岸等沿海防护措施的增加有助于限制1997-98年和2015-16年其他非常大的厄尔尼诺现象期间的侵蚀，沿着幸运的时机，大浪在每月潮汐周期的低点到达，导致财产损失明显低于1982-83年。

paragraphs.en: The coast was not so fortunate in winter 2022-23, when high seas and waves alone caused an estimated $4.7 billion in economic losses along California’s coast. The simultaneous occurrence of large storm waves, high tides and elevated sea levels were almost identical to the El Niño conditions in early 1983, 40 years earlier.
paragraphs.zh: 2022- 2023年冬季，海岸就没那么幸运了，当时仅公海和海浪就沿着加州海岸造成了约47亿美元的经济损失，大风暴浪、涨潮和海平面上升同时发生，与40年前1983年初的厄尔尼诺情况几乎一模一样。

paragraphs.en: The state’s latest climate assessment, released Oct. 19, 2026, warns of more intense storms and increased erosion as temperatures increase and sea level continues to rise.
paragraphs.zh: 该州于2026年10月19日发布的最新气候评估警告说，随着气温上升和海平面继续上升，风暴将更加强烈，侵蚀将加剧。

paragraphs.en: The El Niño of 2026-27
paragraphs.zh: 2026- 2027年的厄尔尼诺现象

paragraphs.en: What will California see in 2026-27?
paragraphs.zh: 2026-27年加州会看到什么？

paragraphs.en: The southern end of the state is already suffering wave damage from an exceptionally busy Pacific hurricane season, also fueled by El Niño. Swells have stripped away beaches and destroyed homes in Southern California. The state’s storm season, when powerful atmospheric rivers bring downpours, typically begins in October or November and runs through early spring.
paragraphs.zh: 加州南端已经遭受了异常繁忙的忙碌季节带来的海浪破坏，厄尔尼诺现象也助长了这种情况。巨浪已经冲毁了南加州的海滩，摧毁了房屋。加州的风暴季节通常从10月或11月开始，伴随着强大的大气河流带来倾盆大雨，一直持续到早春。

paragraphs.en: The magnitude of the emerging 2026-27 El Niño, likely to be one of the strongest on record, is making clear that coastal communities need to adapt now to a very different future.
paragraphs.zh: 2026- 2027年出现的厄尔尼诺现象可能是有记录以来最强的厄尔尼诺现象之一，这表明沿海社区现在需要适应一个非常不同的未来。

paragraphs.en: How each coastal neighborhood, city and county responds will vary depending upon their local conditions and vulnerability to coastal erosion and flooding.
paragraphs.zh: 每个沿海社区、城市和县的反应将取决于当地的条件和对海岸侵蚀和洪水的脆弱性。

paragraphs.en: While many communities are stockpiling sandbags, clearing culverts and preparing evacuation plans, there are limits on what they can do to stop erosion. Building seawalls and rock revetments can provide some protection if well designed, but they can also create new problems, including leading to the loss of beaches over time as sea levels continue to rise. Putting more sand on beaches is costly and very short-lived.
paragraphs.zh: 虽然许多社区都在囤积沙袋、清理涵洞、准备疏散计划，但他们在阻止侵蚀方面所能做的是有限的。如果设计得当，修建海堤和岩石护岸可以提供一些保护，但它们也会带来新的问题，包括随着海平面的持续上升，随着时间的推移，海滩会消失。在海滩上放更多的沙子成本高昂，而且寿命很短。

paragraphs.en: Extensive shoreline development, eroding bluffs, aging infrastructure and increasing exposure to extreme weather are placing growing pressure on coastal communities and shorelines around the world. Some will eventually face the difficult transition from continued shoreline protection to retreating from the coast – either planned retreat or following repeated damage.
paragraphs.zh: 大规模的海岸线开发、悬崖侵蚀、基础设施老化以及极端天气的日益暴露，正在给世界各地的沿海社区和海岸线带来越来越大的压力。一些社区和海岸线最终将面临从继续保护海岸线到从海岸线撤退的艰难过渡--要么是计划中的撤退，要么是在一再遭受破坏之后撤退。

paragraphs.en: There is little that any developed coastal area can do at this point to minimize the impacts of the El Niño underway. What they can do is prepare to manage the risks and try to adapt to the changing future.
paragraphs.zh: 在这一点上，任何发达的沿海地区都无法最大限度地减少厄尔尼诺现象的影响。他们所能做的是准备管理风险，并努力适应不断变化的未来。
